The simple answer is that 𝑋𝑖∼Bin(10, 0.5) is symmetric, so there are no asymmetries
to overcome as you add samples together. In fact, you can view, say, 3 Bin(10, 0.5) as 30
Ber(0.5).
e. Recall that sampling theory allows a reasonably large sample to stand in for the true
population distribution. When resampling from the sample for bootstrapping purposes, we
generally do so with replacement. Why with replacement instead of without?
We sample with replacement because we treat the original set of samples as a probability
mass function. If we were to sample without replacement, we’re incapable of creating
resamples of a size larger than the original sample, and when the size of the resample is
close to the size of the original, each resample would essentially be a replica of the original.

    return [flu, und, fev, tir]
